newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Oil giant Shell cautious on outlook.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Oil giant Shell cautious on outlook.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group issued a cautious outlook for oil prices and refining margins on Thursday as it reported flat first-quarter profits.

The Anglo-Dutch oil giant warned that oil prices may remain under pressure after they started falling in February. Shell said production increases in both OPEC and non-OPEC countries are likely to exceed demand growth, while global inventories are projected to rise.
The company, which is 60 percent owned by Royal Dutch Petroleum and 40 percent by Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc, added it also expected refining margins to remain under pressure.

A modest first-quarter recovery in chemicals may continue in the second quarter, but the longer-term outlook depended on the ability of derivative product prices to recover the increase in product prices.
Overall first-quarter earnings excluding special items edged up one percent to 1.545 billion pounds ($2.5 billion) from 1.535 billion a year ago, coming in at the centre of analysts' expectations.
The rise was held back by the pound's strength, with Shell saying the profit increase would have been seven percent when measured in dollars.
The company said it was pleased with the overall result considering that the 1996 first quarter was boosted by exceptionally cold winter weather in the northern hemisphere.
"We see this as a good result, particularly if you take into consideration that the 1996 first-quarter was a very good quarter," a Shell spokesman said.
First-quarter earnings in the exploration and production sector rose nine percent to 996 million pounds, but the impact of higher oil prices was partly offset by lower gas volumes.
In refining, earnings were one percent down at 519 million pounds. Lower profits in the United States were largely offset by an improved performance elsewhere in the world.

The average Rotterdam complex refining margin was comparable to the level in the first 1996 quarter, Shell said. Winter demand provided strength to distillate prices, while gasoline prices were relatively depressed.
But the complex margin was substantially down in Singapore after distillate prices there were very strong a year ago due to low inventories.
Chemicals earnings rose 12 percent to 184 million pounds due to further cost cutting, which more than compensated for lower margins, Shell said.
The company reported a bigger loss for corporate items such as taxation and service fees, partly due to currency exchange losses.
Shares in Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc fell nine pence to 1,081 pence following Shell's careful outlook. Royal Dutch shares were down 1.10 at 347.10 guilders in Amsterdam.
"There are the usual cautious mutterings about the second half with supply upstream and downstream likely to be plentiful and prices and margins under pressure," one analyst said.
